info.name: NovaBank API
info.description:
Functional API coverage for NovaBank, organised as journeys rather than as endpoint-by-endpoint checks.

Each folder tells a story whose steps depend on one another: the account, the beneficiary, the opening balance and the resulting transfer reference are all carried forward from the request that produced them. That chaining is what this collection contributes that the REST Assured suite does not — that suite owns the authorization matrix, the response schemas and the regression sweep, which are awkward to express here.

Folders 00 and 05 are read-only and safe against any environment. The rest create data, move money or change state, so point them at a local or CI database. Folders 07, 09 and 10 restore what they changed, so they can be run repeatedly.

Any folder carrying a pre-request script can be run on its own: it establishes the session, and where needed the beneficiary, that its requests depend on.

Run everything with Newman:

    npm run test

Sign-in is two steps everywhere: credentials raise an MFA challenge, and the challenge is exchanged for a session. With QA_MODE on, the one-time code comes back in the response, so no mail server is needed.

item.name: 07 Credential recovery
item.description:
Forgotten and changed passwords, end to end. Security-critical and, before this folder, untested anywhere in the project.

Uses the receiver identity rather than the primary customer, so a run that changes a password cannot lock the other folders out of their session. The password is restored at the end.

item.name: 08 Card lifecycle
item.description:
A card through its whole state machine: requested, activated, frozen, unfrozen, reconfigured, replaced, cancelled.

Each step asserts the state it produced and, where the machine forbids a move, that the move is refused. The card action endpoints return the customer's whole card list rather than the single card, so every assertion locates its own card by id.

item.name: 10 Currency and limits
item.description:
Cross-currency conversion and the daily transfer ceiling.

Both were reachable but unexercised: fx_rate and credited_amount_minor appeared only in a schema, and daily_limit_minor only as a field name. BUG-DB-001 was about the precision of the first of those, so until now its regression check was a column type rather than a conversion.
